content:
Hello there


You mentioned that you are seeing a block when trying to retrieve your email. The padlock icon you see next to the envelope is a standard symbol indicating that your connection is secure and encrypted.

This icon is always there and is nothing to worry about—it does not mean your account is locked.

An actual account block usually happens when your email provider’s security system steps in, such as after too many failed login attempts or due to unusual activity.

Fortunately, this is easy to fix. Here is how you can resolve it:


1. Log in via webmail: Open your internet browser and sign in to your email online (rather than using the Thunderbird program). You will often see a prompt right away to unlock your account.

2. Reset your password if needed: If prompted, create a new password online and then update it in Thunderbird as well.


Do you not see any prompt online?

Please check your saved passwords in Thunderbird by going to: Settings > Privacy & Security > Saved Passwords.

If this does not solve the issue, it could be caused by a frozen session within Thunderbird itself.

Please try the steps above first and let me know if it worked, and I will be happy to assist you further


.

content: THunderbird has two releases: the monthly (now 160), and the extended support release (ESR, now 153.7). The ESR release gets one major update a year and minor fixes throughout the year. This version does not get the latest new features until next release but it is the more stable version. If stability is important, this is the release to use. If you want the very latest stuff, then use the monthly. The default download at thunderbird.net is the monthly, but the ESR is also there.

content:
You should never try to change and existing IMAP account in Thunderbird to POP or vice versa. The safe method is to create another account alongside the existing one.

If you're talking about the Export tool found in the Tools menu, it makes a copy of your entire Profile folder. It's basically the same as manually copying the profile folder. When you import a backed up folder using the Import tool and it finds existing folders it will make a new folder alongside of it. It will not overwrite them.

You could, instead, manually restore a profile folder with a previously backed up copy of it, in which case you would be in the same state as when you made the backup.
